findings.title: Raw substring check enables upsampling for non-error Discover queries
findings.body: The Discover eligibility check treats any query containing the text `event.type:error` as error-only. This is not a semantic query check: for example, `!event.type:error` (a supported syntax used elsewhere in this endpoint) contains that substring but explicitly selects non-error events, and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` selects transactions as well. Those queries will be rewritten to sum `sample_weight`, even though transactions/non-error events do not have error sampling weights, producing failed queries or incorrect counts. Determine event-type constraints from the parsed query and require that the query cannot include non-error event types.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, but eligibility is evaluated against the `dataset` captured from the original request. In the dashboard split path, an enhanced-metrics widget can call `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., errors_only_query, ...)` while the captured dataset is a metrics dataset. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` rejects metrics datasets, so this explicitly error-only Discover subquery is never upsampled despite all projects being allowlisted. Evaluate eligibility against `scoped_dataset` and the actual `query` argument rather than the original request context.

findings.title: The internal upsampling aggregate is exposed to client queries
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is registered without `private=True`, unlike the adjacent internal aggregate. As a result, clients can request `upsampled_count()` directly through Discover/Event Stats without passing the allowlist and event-type checks in `error_upsampling.py`. This permits unallowlisted or mixed-event queries to use `sample_weight`, yielding unsupported/incorrect results (or query failures where the field is unavailable). Mark the function private and expose it only through the guarded rewrite.

findings.title: Upsampled counts truncate fractional sampling weights
findings.body: The implementation applies `toInt64` to `sum(sample_weight)`. Sampling rates are floats (the added test factory explicitly converts `client_sample_rate` to float), so weights such as `1 / 0.3` and sums of heterogeneous weights are not necessarily integral. Casting the final sum to an integer truncates the estimate and systematically underreports error counts. Return the numeric sum directly, or use the established rounding behavior for sampled-count estimates if the API contract requires integral counts.
